setting.name: fusionSettingFormat
setting.description: The format of this settings file. Change it and the next compile writes the settings in the new format and keeps the old file as a backup (.bak) - only one settings file is active

setting.name: tabWidth
setting.description: How many spaces a tab counts as

setting.name: allowMixed
setting.description: Allow tabs and spaces mixed in one file's indentation

section.name: source
section.description: What the source text may contain

setting.name: allowUnicodeIdentifiers
setting.description: Allow letters beyond ASCII in names (a security risk: look-alike letters)

setting.name: caseSensitive
setting.description: count and Count are two names; false: names that differ only in case are an error, each pair listed

setting.name: maxNestingDepth
setting.description: How deeply structs may hold structs (1 = no struct inside another)

setting.name: warnNestingDepth
setting.description: Warn from this depth (0 = never warn)

setting.name: stringStorage
setting.description: How a string field holds its text

setting.name: stringMutable
setting.description: A string field can be changed after the struct is made

setting.name: stringWarnLength
setting.description: Warn when a string field's text is longer than this (0 = never warn)

setting.name: functions
setting.description: Methods written inside a struct (p.move(1, 2) changes p); false: a function inside a struct is an error

setting.name: holdCollections
setting.description: A struct field may be a List or a Map; false makes such a field an error

setting.name: maxLength
setting.description: The longest a string may be, in characters - longer is an error, never cut

setting.name: encoding
setting.description: How text is stored

setting.name: nullBecomesEmpty
setting.description: A string is never null: s = null makes s "" - false (the default): s = null is a compile error, nothing changes silently (D.138, D.003)

setting.name: layer
setting.description: std: everything; alloc: no operating system (no print, files); core: no memory allocation

setting.name: returns
setting.description: Error returns: T, Error function and capturing T x, err = f()

setting.name: exceptions
setting.description: try / catch / finally / throw

setting.name: autoWidening
setting.description: An int used as a float widens automatically (with a warning); false: it must fit exactly

setting.name: overflowWrap
setting.description: Whole-number + - * wraps around (a byte: 255 + 1 is 0); false: it is an OverflowError

setting.name: rounding
setting.description: How a decimal is rounded when a result has more places than it keeps (* past 18 places, / that doesn't end, round without a mode): halfEven (banker's - no drift over many sums), halfUp, down (toward zero), up (away from zero), exact (rounding needed is a RoundingError) (D.177)

setting.name: variables
setting.description: Module-level variables (module constants are always allowed)

section.name: collections
section.description: Arrays, Lists, Maps and collection classes

setting.name: allowChangeWhileLooping
setting.description: A collection class of your own may be changed inside a loop over it (its own rules decide); false: blocked - Fusion's own arrays, Lists and Maps never are

setting.name: stackWarn
setting.description: A plain or fixed array on the stack larger than this: a warning - also the line between a small and a large array; lower it for a small embedded device (e.g. "1KB") (D.145)

setting.name: order
setting.description: Which dimension a loop and length give first, and how the slots lie in memory: columns - the outer dimension first, depth then columns then rows (as Fortran, MATLAB, Julia, R); rows - rows then columns then depth (as C, Java, C#, Python); depthRows - depth then rows then columns (on 2 dimensions the same as rows) (D.148)

setting.name: stackLimit
setting.description: A plain or fixed array on the stack larger than this: a compile error - a growable array (int:[]) or a List lives on the heap instead (D.145)

setting.name: csvManyDimensions
setting.description: toCSV on an array of 3 dimensions: each line holds that row of every sheet side by side, the sheets split by the secondary delimiter ("#"); false: a compile error (D.151)

setting.name: storage
setting.description: How an array of 2 or 3 dimensions is stored: flat - one block (the default, fastest for matrices); rect - comes later (D.164); a jagged array is set per array, a.setStorage(JAGG) on a growable one (D.144, D.153)

section.name: generics
section.description: Generic functions and types of the program's own

setting.name: enabled
setting.description: Generic functions, structs and classes of the program's own (T function first<T>(List<T> items)); false: a generic declaration is a compile error - the built-in List<T> and Map<K, V> stay (D.168)

setting.name: sharedStatics
setting.description: A generic class's statics: false - one set per copy (Box<int>.made and Box<string>.made are separate, a static of type T allowed); true - one set for all copies, written Box.made (a static of type T an error) (D.173)

section.name: ranges
section.description: Ranges in a loop: for i in 0...13 step 5

setting.name: strictStep
setting.description: A range's step that doesn't land on its end (0...13 step 5 gives 0 5 10): false - a warning, only the values within the range run; true - a compile error (D.170)

setting.name: decimals
setting.description: Ranges over float, double, decimal and money (for x in 0.5...2.5 step 0.5): false - an error saying how to turn them on; true - allowed, each value worked out from its count (start + n * step), never by adding, so nothing drifts (D.170)

setting.name: stepRequired
setting.description: A range of decimals must write its step: true - 0.5...2.5 without a step is an error; false - it uses defaultStep (D.170)

setting.name: defaultStep
setting.description: The step of a range of decimals written without one, when stepRequired is false (D.170)

setting.name: rangeMaxStep
setting.description: How many places a range's finest step has: 3 - 0.001 (or -0.001); a finer step is an error, written or while running - no huge or endless range by mistake; science and engineering projects raise it (D.170)

setting.name: ownership
setting.description: strict (the default, the safest): every ownership rule - Car b = a hands the object over (a can't be used until it gets a new value), one writer, a borrow never stored or returned; relaxed: Car b = a shares one object, the rules loosened - for a library with no ownership model (a GC alongside it) or manual memory. byVal copies and byRef borrows in both. Replaces assignment (move / share), still read with a warning (D.124)

setting.name: moveFieldOut
setting.description: A field may be moved out of a struct the function owns, as in Rust - the struct can't be used afterwards until it gets a new value; false: a struct's fields are only borrowed, never taken out (D.026)

setting.name: defaultMethods
setting.description: An interface's function may have code, used by a class that doesn't give its own; false: an interface names its functions only

setting.name: required
setting.description: Writing public / internal / private on every top-level item and class member is mandatory; false: nothing written means its default (fields and module variables private, the rest public)

setting.name: numbers
setting.description: A number as a condition - positive: above zero is true; nonzero: not zero is true (C, Python); off: a condition must be a bool

setting.name: notAroundGuard
setting.description: '!' around a ?. test - if !(x?.age >= 18) - turns unknown into yes; false (the default): a compile error, test null on its own (if x is null ... else if ...); true: allowed with a warning (D.116)

setting.name: mode
setting.description: safe; strict: every warning is an error (security, no undetermined behaviour); unsafe: the whole project may take direct control (memory, assembly, devices)

setting.name: maxCallDepth
setting.description: How deep calls may go; max: endless recursion is caught by stack use alone

setting.name: waitAtExit
setting.description: Wait for a key before the window closes, so the output can be read - for development, examples and testing, or an app that shows its details to the customer (never with --headless)

setting.name: target
setting.description: c: C compiled by GCC
